sections.title: 1. Program structure and compiling
sections.md:
A program = one or more `.c` files + `.h` headers; exactly one defines `main`. Two legal forms: `int main(void)` and `int main(int argc, char *argv[])`. Falling off the end of `main` returns 0.

```c
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
int main(int argc, char *argv[]) {
    if (argc != 2) {                       // argv[0] is the program name
        fprintf(stderr, "Usage: %s n\n", argv[0]);
        return 1;                          // non-zero exit status = failure
    }
    int n = atoi(argv[1]);                 // "21" -> 21 (atof for double)
    printf("%d\n", n * 2);
    return 0;
}
```

- `argc` counts the program name: `./prog` alone gives `argc == 1`; `argv[1]`..`argv[argc - 1]` are the arguments (strings); `argv[argc]` is `NULL`. Check `argc` **before** touching `argv[i]`.
- Errors/usage go to `stderr` with `fprintf(stderr, ...)`, then exit non-zero. `return n` in `main` (or `exit(n)` anywhere, `<stdlib.h>`) sets the status; Bash shows it with `echo $?`.
- `puts(s)` adds a `'\n'`; `printf` prints exactly what you give it.

### gcc's four stages
| stage | does | stop with | output |
|---|---|---|---|
| preprocess | `#include` pastes the header text, removes comments | `-E` | `.i` (a *translation unit*) |
| compile | C to assembly | `-S` | `.s` |
| assemble | assembly to object code | `-c` | `.o` |
| link | joins `.o` files + the C library | (default) | `a.out` or `-o name` |

- Headers give **declarations** only; the code for `printf` arrives at **link** time from the standard library.
- `gcc -std=c17 -Wall -o prog prog.c` then `./prog` (the current folder is not in `PATH`). Several files: `gcc -Wall -o demo demo.c qlstack.c`, or `gcc -c a.c`, `gcc -c b.c`, `gcc a.o b.o -o prog`.
- **Math library: `-lm` goes AFTER the source file**: `gcc -Wall -o sin sin.c -lm`. The linker reads left to right, so `gcc -o sin -lm sin.c` fails on Ubuntu with ``undefined reference to `pow'`` (same message if `-lm` is missing).
- `undefined reference` / `multiple definition` = **linker** errors (missing or duplicate definition). `file:line:col: error:` = compiler error, no program made; `warning:` = program made but probably buggy: fix every one.
- `-o` overwrites: `gcc -o first.c second.c` destroys `first.c`.

sections.title: 2. Types, printf and scanf formats
sections.md:
| type | bytes (64-bit Linux) | printf | scanf |
|---|---|---|---|
| `char` | 1 | `%c` (char), `%d` (its code) | `%c` (`" %c"` skips spaces) |
| `short` | 2 | `%hd` | `%hd` |
| `int` / `unsigned int` | 4 | `%d` or `%i` / `%u` | `%d` / `%u` |
| `long` / `unsigned long` | 8 | `%ld` / `%lu` | `%ld` / `%lu` |
| `long long` | 8 | `%lld` / `%llu` | `%lld` |
| `size_t` (unsigned; `sizeof`, `strlen`) | 8 | `%zu` | `%zu` |
| `ptrdiff_t` (pointer difference) | 8 | `%td` | |
| `float` | 4 | `%f` | `%f` |
| `double` | 8 | `%f` `%e` `%g` | **`%lf`** |
| `long double` | 16 | `%Lf` | `%Lf` |
| any pointer | 8 | `%p` with `(void *) p` | |
| `bool` (`<stdbool.h>`, 0/1) | 1 | `%d` | |
| string (`char *`) | | `%s` | `%s` (one word, array, no `&`) |

The standard fixes only **minimums** (char 8 bits, short/int 16, long 32, long long 64) and the order `1 == sizeof(char) <= short <= int <= long <= long long`.

```c
printf("[%5d][%-5d][%05d]\n", 42, 42, 42);  // [   42][42   ][00042]
printf("[%.2f][%8.3f]\n", 3.14159, 3.14159); // [3.14][   3.142]
printf("[%e][%g]\n", 3.14159, 3.14159);      // [3.141590e+00][3.14159]
printf("[%.3s][%x][%02X][%o]\n", "CISC220", 255, 10, 8); // [CIS][ff][0A][10]
printf("%c %d %zu%%\n", 'A', 'A', sizeof(int));        // A 65 4%
```

- Width = minimum width, right-aligned (`-` left-aligns, `0` pads with zeros); never truncates numbers. `.n` = digits after the point for `%f`/`%e`, significant digits for `%g`, max chars for `%s`. `%f` = `%.6f`. `%24.17f` = 17 decimals, at least 24 wide. `%%` prints `%`. `%x`/`%X` hex, `%o` octal.
- A conversion that does not match the argument type is **undefined behaviour**; `-Wall` warns.
- Escapes: `\n` `\t` `\\` `\"` `\'` `\0`. `'A'` is a `char` (65), `"A"` is a string (2 chars).
- `enum day { sun, mon };` gives `sun == 0`, `mon == 1`; `enum month { jan = 1, feb };` gives `feb == 2`. Plain ints, no type safety.
- `const double PI = 3.14159;` is read-only: assigning it is a compile error. `void` = no value (`void f(void)`); `sizeof(void)` is an error.

```c
int n; double d; char word[10]; char c;
int got = scanf("%d %lf %9s %c", &n, &d, word, &c); // word: no &
if (got != 4) {
    fprintf(stderr, "bad input\n");
    return 1;
}
printf("%d %.1f %s %c\n", n, d, word, c);  // printf: %f for double
```

- `scanf`/`sscanf`/`fscanf` return the number of values **assigned**, `EOF` if input ended before the first conversion. Every receiving argument is a pointer (`&n`); an array name already is one.

sections.title: 3. Scope, lifetime and static
4. Declarations, functions, headers, statements
sections.md:
- **Declaration** = a name exists and has this type; **definition** = also creates it (a variable's storage, a function's body). `int a = -5, b, c = 5;` initialises only `a` and `c`. `const` is part of the type.
- Prototype = header + `;`: `double max2(double x, double y);`. Declare before use (prototype above, or define above `main`); otherwise `implicit declaration of function` and then `conflicting types`. Zero parameters: write `(void)`.
- Arguments are passed **by value** (copies), structs too. Arrays decay to a pointer to element 0.
- Read declarations from the name: right first (`[]` array of, `()` function returning), then left (`*` pointer to). `int *p, q;`: only `p` is a pointer. `int *a[3]`: array of 3 `int *`. `int (*f)(int)`: pointer to function.
- No access modifiers; all functions have **external linkage** (one definition per program) unless `static`.

```c
// max2.h
#ifndef MAX2_H
#define MAX2_H
double max2(double x, double y);    // declaration (prototype)
#endif
```

- Put declarations in `name.h` inside an **include guard**; `#include "max2.h"` in both `max2.c` and every user. **Never `#include "max2.c"`**: `max2` gets defined twice (`multiple definition`). `<...>` = system header, `"..."` = your own.

### Statements (as in Java, except...)
- No `boolean`: a condition is false if 0, true otherwise; `==`, `<` ... give `1` or `0`. `&&` and `||` short-circuit.
- `switch` only on integers (incl. `char`, `enum`); cases fall through without `break`.
- `for`, `while`, `do { } while (c);`, `break`, `continue`, `c ? a : b`: same as Java. No enhanced for.
- **Arrays and strings cannot be assigned** (`x = y;` is an error).
- `int / int` truncates toward 0: `7 / 2 == 3`, `-7 / 2 == -3`; `%` takes the sign of the left operand: `-7 % 2 == -1`, `7 % -2 == 1`. `(double) a / b` divides as double; `(double) (a / b)` does not.
- Leading zero = octal: `0123 == 83`. `0x1F == 31`. Suffixes `u`, `L`, `LL`.
- Traps: `if (x = 5)` assigns (always true); without braces only one statement is guarded; `;` after `if (...)` ends the `if`.
- Precedence traps: `==` before `&`/`|`/`^`; `.`/`->`/`[]`/`()`/postfix `++` before unary `*`/`&`; `!=` before `=` (so `c = fgetc(f) != EOF` stores 0/1).

sections.title: 5. Integers: two's complement, overflow, conversions
sections.md:
- `<limits.h>`: `CHAR_BIT` 8, `SCHAR_MIN` -128, `SCHAR_MAX` 127, `UCHAR_MAX` 255, `INT_MAX` 2147483647, `INT_MIN` -2147483648, `UINT_MAX` 4294967295, `LONG_MAX`... `<stdint.h>`: `int8_t`, `uint8_t`, `uint16_t`, `uint32_t`, `int64_t` (exact widths).
- `char`, `signed char`, `unsigned char` are three types; plain `char` is signed or unsigned (implementation-defined; signed on gcc x86). `c - '0'` digit value; `'0' + d` digit char; `'0'` 48, `'A'` 65, `'a'` 97.

### Unsigned and two's complement (n bits)
- Unsigned: bit i is worth 2^i; range 0 .. 2^n - 1 (8 bits: 0..255).
- Two's complement: the top bit is worth **-2^(n-1)**; range -2^(n-1) .. 2^(n-1) - 1 (8 bits: -128..127). `01101011` = 107, `11101011` = -128+64+32+8+2+1 = **-21**, `11111111` = -1, `10000000` = -128, `01111111` = 127.
- Negate: **flip all bits and add 1** (`~x + 1 == -x`): 56 = `00111000` → `11000111` + 1 = `11001000` = -56. Fails only for the most negative value.
- Ones' complement (Day 5): negate = flip; two zeros (`00000000`, `11111111`); range -127..127; addition adds an end-around carry. Two's complement: one zero, a carry out of the top is dropped.
- Asymmetric range: `-x`, `abs(x)`, `-1 * x`, `x / -1` do not exist for `x == INT_MIN`: **UB**. `abs`, `labs`, `llabs` are in `<stdlib.h>` (not `<math.h>`).

### Overflow and conversions
- **Unsigned** arithmetic wraps modulo 2^n (defined). **Signed** overflow (`INT_MAX + 1`) is **undefined**: check first or use a wider type.
- To unsigned: value modulo 2^n (`(unsigned) -1 == UINT_MAX`; 300 into `uint8_t` = 44). Out-of-range value to a signed type: implementation-defined (gcc wraps: 200 into `signed char` = -56).
- **Integer promotion**: `char`, `short` (and `uint8_t`) become `int` in any arithmetic.
- **Usual arithmetic conversions**: `int` op `unsigned int` → unsigned; anything op `double` → `double`. So `-1 < 1u` is **false**, and `size_t` maths can wrap.
- `double` → integer drops the fraction (toward 0: `(int) -2.7 == -2`); if the value does not fit: UB.

```c
unsigned int u = UINT_MAX;
u = u + 1;                            // unsigned wraps mod 2^32: 0
int big = 300;
uint8_t b = big;                      // 300 mod 256 = 44
signed char sc = -128;                // bits 10000000
printf("%u %d %d\n", u, b, ~sc + 1);  // 0 44 128 (promoted to int)
printf("%d\n", -1 < 1u);              // 0: -1 becomes UINT_MAX
printf("%zu\n", strlen("") - 1);      // 18446744073709551615
printf("%d %d %d\n", -7 / 2, -7 % 2, (int) -2.7);  // -3 -1 -2
```

sections.title: 6. Bitwise operations and masks
sections.md:
| op | bit rule | identities | mask use |
|---|---|---|---|
| `~x` NOT | flip | ones' complement; `~x + 1 == -x` | |
| `x & m` AND | 1 if both 1 | `b & 0 = 0`, `b & 1 = b` | **keep/test/clear** bits |
| `x \| m` OR | 1 if either 1 | `b \| 0 = b`, `b \| 1 = 1` | **set** bits |
| `x ^ m` XOR | 1 if different | `b ^ 0 = b`, `b ^ 1 = ~b` (notebook typo writes `\|`) | **toggle** bits |
| `x << k` | move left, 0s in on the right, top bits lost | `x * 2^k` if nothing lost | build masks |
| `x >> k` | move right, low bits lost | unsigned: `x / 2^k` (floor) | extract fields |

```c
void printb(uint8_t x) {              // prints 8 bits, MSB first
    char buf[9];
    for (size_t i = 0; i < 8; i++) {
        buf[7 - i] = (x & (1u << i)) ? '1' : '0';
    }
    buf[8] = '\0';
    printf("%s\n", buf);
}

uint8_t x = 18, y = 206;              // 00010010, 11001110
printb(x & y);                        // 00000010
printb(x | y);                        // 11011110
printb(x ^ y);                        // 11011100
uint8_t nx = ~x;                      // store back to keep 8 bits
printf("%d %d\n", nx, ~x);            // 237 -19 (~x alone is an int)
printf("%d %d\n", 23 << 2, 23 >> 2);  // 92 5
```

```c
unsigned int x = 0xF0;                // 1111 0000
unsigned int k = 1;
x |= 1u << k;                         // set bit 1      -> 0xF2
x &= ~(1u << 4);                      // clear bit 4    -> 0xE2
x ^= 1u << 7;                         // toggle bit 7   -> 0x62
unsigned int bit5 = (x >> 5) & 1u;    // test bit 5     -> 1
unsigned int low3 = x & ((1u << 3) - 1);  // low 3 bits -> 2
printf("%X %u %u\n", x, bit5, low3);  // 62 1 2
if ((x & 1u) == 0) {                  // brackets: == binds tighter than &
    puts("even");
}
printf("%c%c%c\n", 'A' | 32, 'b' & ~32, 'q' ^ 32);  // aBQ
```

- Idioms: test bit k `(x >> k) & 1u`; set `x |= 1u << k`; clear `x &= ~(1u << k)`; toggle `x ^= 1u << k`; n low ones `(1u << n) - 1`; extract field `(x >> pos) & mask`; replace field `x = (x & ~(mask << pos)) | (v << pos)`. Odd test `x & 1` (works for negatives in two's complement).
- Letters differ from the other case only in bit 5 (32): `c | 32` lower, `c & ~32` upper, `c ^ 32` toggle (letters only).
- **Use unsigned types and `1u` for bit work.** UB: shift count negative or **≥ width** (32 for `int`); signed `<<` that overflows (e.g. `1 << 31`). Implementation-defined: `>>` of a **negative** value (gcc: arithmetic, copies the sign bit: `-45 >> 2 == -12`, while `-45 / 4 == -11`). Unsigned `>>` is logical (0s in).
- Logical shift = 0s come in; arithmetic right shift = copies of the sign bit come in (floor division by 2^k).
- Promotion: on a `uint8_t` the result of `~`, `<<` is an `int`; it is cut to 8 bits only when stored back (`(uint8_t)(23 << 4) == 112`).
- `&`/`|` work per bit; `&&`/`||` are logical: with `a = 2, b = 4`, `a & b == 0` but `a && b == 1`. One hex digit = 4 bits, one octal digit = 3 bits (`chmod 754` = `0754`).

sections.title: 7. Floating point
sections.md:
- `float` (4 bytes, ~7 significant digits, literal `0.1f`), `double` (8 bytes, ~15-16 digits, literal `0.1`, the default), `long double`. IEEE 754 binary formats, same as Java. Limits in `<float.h>` (`FLT_MAX`, `DBL_EPSILON`).
- Most decimal fractions are **not exact** in binary: `0.1f` is 0.1000000015. Never compare with `==`/`!=` and never control a loop with them; compare with a tolerance `fabs(a - b) <= tol` (relative: `tol * fmax(fabs(a), fabs(b))`); count loops with an `int`.

```c
double a = 0.1 + 0.2;
printf("%.17f\n", a);                     // 0.30000000000000004
printf("%d %d\n", a == 0.3, fabs(a - 0.3) < 1e-9);   // 0 1
double zero = 0.0;
double inf = 1.0 / zero, nan = zero / zero;  // no crash for doubles
printf("%d %d %d\n", isinf(inf), isnan(nan), nan == nan); // 1 1 0
printf("%d %.1f %d\n", 1 / 2, 1.0 / 2, (int) 3.99);      // 0 0.5 3
printf("%f %g\n", sqrt(2.0), pow(2, 10));  // 1.414214 1024
```

- `1.0 / 0.0` is `inf`, `0.0 / 0.0` is NaN (glibc prints `-nan`); `INFINITY`, `NAN`, `isinf`, `isnan` from `<math.h>`. `d == INFINITY` works; **`NAN == NAN` is false**. Integer division by 0 is **UB** (usually a crash).
- `<math.h>`: `sqrt`, `pow`, `fabs`, `fmax`, `sin`/`cos` (radians), `floor`, `ceil`; no overloading, so `sinf` (float), `sin` (double), `sinl` (long double). Link with **`-lm` after the `.c` file**.
- `%f` fixed (6 decimals by default), `%e` scientific, `%g` the shorter, 6 significant digits; `.n` precision rounds. `float` arguments are promoted to `double` in `printf`, so `%f` prints both; `scanf` needs `%f` for `float *` and `%lf` for `double *`.
- Mixed `int`/`double` arithmetic is done in `double`; `1 / 2` is still `0` (both int) and `1.0 / 2` is `0.5`. Factorials and big powers: use `double`, not `int` (13! overflows `int`).

sections.title: 8. Pointers
sections.md:
- A pointer holds the **address** of an object. `T *p` = pointer to `T` (8 bytes here). `&x` = address of `x`; `*p` = the object `p` points at (read `y = *p;`, write `*p = 5;`). Memory is byte addressable; an object's address is that of its first byte.
- `int *p, *q;` (a `*` on each name). Draw a memory table (name, address, value) or boxes and arrows; update it line by line.
- `p = q;` copies an **address** (now both point at the same object). `*p = *q;` copies a **value**.
- `NULL` (`<stddef.h>`, also `<stdio.h>`, `<stdlib.h>`) = no object. The only safe things to do with it: test `p == NULL`, `!p`, `p != NULL`, `if (p)`. Initialise every pointer (`= &x` or `= NULL`).
- **UB**: dereferencing `NULL`, an uninitialised pointer, or a dangling one (object dead or freed). Often "Segmentation fault", sometimes silent.
- `void *` holds any object pointer without a cast, but must be converted before use: `int y = *((int *) p);` or `const int *ip = p;`. The cast must match the real type.
- Equal pointers (`==`): both `NULL`, same object, array vs its first element, struct vs its first member, both too-far in one array. `<`, `<=`, `-` only within one array.

```c
void swap(int *x, int *y) {     // gets addresses
    int tmp = *x;               // tmp is an int, not a pointer
    *x = *y;
    *y = tmp;
}
int main(void) {
    int a = 1, b = 2;
    int *p = &a, *q = &b;       // * on EACH name
    swap(&a, &b);               // a = 2, b = 1
    *p = *p + 10;               // a = 12; to add 1 write (*p)++, not *p++
    p = q;                      // p now points at b
    printf("%d %d %d\n", a, b, *p);   // 12 1 1
    return 0;
}
```

- To change a caller's variable of type `T`: parameter `T *x`, use `*x` inside, call `f(&v)`. Assigning to `x` itself only changes the local copy.
- Output parameter: declare a real variable and pass its address: `size_t i; max(arr, 9, &i);`. Passing `size_t *i;` (uninitialised) is UB.
- `(*p)++` increments the value; `*p++` moves the pointer (and `-Wall` warns the value is unused).
- `const int *p`: cannot change `*p` through `p`; `int *const p`: cannot change `p`. `const char *s` in a prototype = "only reads the string".
- Passing a pointer copies 8 bytes instead of a big object (arrays, structs).

15. File I/O
sections.md:
`<stdio.h>`. A stream is a source/sink of chars, represented by the opaque `FILE`; you only ever hold `FILE *`. `stdin`, `stdout`, `stderr` are open when `main` starts. Buffering: `stderr` unbuffered, `stdout`/`stdin` line buffered on a terminal, files fully buffered (`fflush(f)` pushes output out).

| mode | opens for | if it exists | if not |
|---|---|---|---|
| `"r"` | reading | start at 0 | **fails** (`NULL`) |
| `"w"` | writing | **erased** | created |
| `"a"` | appending (every write at the end) | kept | created |
| `"r+"` / `"w+"` / `"a+"` | read and write (update) | as above | as above |

```c
FILE *f = fopen("io_test.txt", "r");      // "w" would erase it!
if (!f) {
    perror("fopen failed");
    exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
}
int c;                                    // int, not char: EOF is an int
int count = 0;
while ((c = fgetc(f)) != EOF) {           // inner brackets matter
    count++;
}
printf("%d %d %ld\n", count, feof(f) != 0, ftell(f));   // 11 1 11
rewind(f);                                // or fseek(f, 0, SEEK_SET)
char line[100];
while (fgets(line, sizeof line, f) != NULL) {  // keeps the '\n'
    size_t len = strlen(line);
    if (len > 0 && line[len - 1] == '\n') {
        line[len - 1] = '\0';
    }
    printf("[%s]", line);                 // [ab][cd][3 xy]
}
fclose(f);
```

| function | returns | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `FILE *fopen(const char *name, const char *mode)` | stream or `NULL` | mode is a string; `perror("msg")` explains `errno` |
| `int fclose(FILE *f)` | 0 or `EOF` | flushes; `f` unusable afterwards; close what you open |
| `int fgetc(FILE *f)` / `getchar()` | next char as `int`, or `EOF` | store in an **`int`** (notebook's `char c` is a slip) |
| `char *fgets(char *buf, int count, FILE *f)` | `buf`, or `NULL` at end/error | at most `count - 1` chars, stops after `'\n'` (kept), adds `'\0'`; long lines come in pieces |
| `int fputc(int c, FILE *f)` / `putchar(c)` | `c` or `EOF` | |
| `int fputs(const char *s, FILE *f)` | ≥ 0 or `EOF` | stream **last**, no newline added |
| `fprintf(f, fmt, ...)` / `fscanf(f, fmt, ...)` | as `printf` / `sscanf` | stream **first**; `fscanf` `%s` reads one word |
| `feof(f)` / `ferror(f)` | non-zero if the end / an error was hit | ask **after** the read loop; `clearerr` resets |
| `long ftell(FILE *f)` | position (bytes from start) | |
| `void rewind(FILE *f)` | | back to position 0 |
| `int fseek(FILE *f, long off, int origin)` | 0, non-zero on failure | `SEEK_SET`, `SEEK_CUR`, `SEEK_END` |

- Pattern: open, test `NULL`, loop `while ((c = fgetc(f)) != EOF)` or `while (fgets(buf, sizeof buf, f) != NULL)`, then `ferror`/`feof`, close; return `EXIT_SUCCESS`/`EXIT_FAILURE`. Line ends are `'\n'` on Linux (each counts as a char).
- `fscanf` loop: `while (fscanf(f, "%d", &x) == 1)`; afterwards `EOF` means end, a smaller count means bad data.
- Update modes: a positioning call (`fseek`, `rewind`) between a read and a write; `fflush` or positioning between a write and a read (`replace_char.c`: `fseek(f, -1, SEEK_CUR); fputc(r, f); fflush(f);`).
- The file position belongs to the stream, not the file. Reading `"yes\n"` with `fgets` then `strcmp(buf, "yes")` fails: strip the `'\n'` first.

sections.title: 16. Undefined behaviour checklist
sections.md:
**UB** = the standard places no requirement: any output, a crash, or "works today". Never give a fixed output for it; answer "undefined behaviour" and why. **Implementation-defined** = each compiler picks and documents one result.

### Undefined
- Reading an uninitialised automatic variable or `malloc`'d memory before writing it.
- Array index or pointer outside `[0, n)` (except forming/comparing the too-far pointer `a + n`); `*(a + n)`.
- Dereferencing `NULL`, an uninitialised pointer, or a dangling pointer (dead local, freed or realloc'd block). Returning a local's address and using it.
- `%s`/`strlen`/`strcpy`/`strcat`/`strcmp` on an unterminated string; destination too small (`strcpy`, `strcat`, `sprintf`, `%s` without width in `scanf`); overlapping `strcpy`, `strcat`, `memcpy`.
- Modifying a string literal.
- Signed overflow (`INT_MAX + 1`, `-INT_MIN`, `abs(INT_MIN)`, `INT_MIN / -1`); integer `/ 0` or `% 0`; `double` to integer out of range.
- Shift by a negative count or ≥ the width; signed `<<` that overflows.
- `printf`/`scanf` conversion not matching the argument type; `scanf` value too big for its type.
- `free` twice, `free` of non-heap or interior pointers, use after `free`.
- Popping/peeking an empty stack (`s->top` is `NULL`); `NULL + 1` from a failed `strchr`.
- Cast a `void *` to the wrong type and dereference it.
- Missing return value used from a non-`void` function (other than `main`).

### Implementation-defined / unspecified (not UB)
- Sizes of types beyond the minimums; whether `char` is signed; `>>` of a negative value; converting an out-of-range value to a signed type; the result of `malloc(0)`.

### Defined (often mistaken for errors)
- Unsigned wrap-around (`UINT_MAX + 1 == 0`); `-1 < 1u` is false; `free(NULL)`; `realloc(NULL, n)`; `1.0 / 0.0` is `inf`; `main` without `return` returns 0.

sections.title: 17. Exam habits (handwritten, closed book)
sections.md:
- **Skeleton first**: `#include`s (`stdio.h`, `stdlib.h`, `string.h`, `stdbool.h`, `math.h` → `-lm` last), helpers above `main` (or prototypes), `int main(int argc, char *argv[])`, `return 0;`. Every `;`, every brace, `;` after a struct's `}`.
- **Function questions**: copy the given header exactly (return type, name, parameter types, `const`). Pointer parameters for results; `&` at the call.
- **Command line**: check `argc` first; usage to `stderr`; exit status 1.
- **Traces**: one column per variable (pointers: what they point at); cross out locals when their block ends; static/global start at 0 once; integer division truncates; `%` sign follows the left operand; `printf` widths count spaces.
- **Strings**: every buffer `strlen + 1`; write the `'\0'`; loops stop at `'\0'`; compare with `strcmp`, copy with `strcpy`/`memcpy`; give `%s`/`%[` a width.
- **Memory**: `sizeof(T)` in every `malloc`, `n * sizeof(T)` for arrays; test for `NULL`; `realloc` into a temporary; count mallocs vs frees (array of 5 strings = 6 of each); free inner blocks first; unlink before free; set `next = NULL` on the last node and `top = NULL` in a new stack.
- **Return values**: check `fopen` (`NULL`), `fgets` (`NULL`), `fgetc` (`EOF`, into an `int`), `sscanf`/`fscanf` (`== count`), `malloc` (`NULL`), `strchr`/`strstr` (`NULL`).
- **Short answers**: say *why* (lifetime ended, decays to a pointer, no room for `'\0'`, shallow copy, overlap needs `memmove`, linker reads left to right). For UB say "undefined behaviour", not a guessed output.
- **Edge cases** before handing in: empty input/list, one element, first and last element, not found, `n == 0`.
- Brackets for safety: `(x & m) == 0`, `(c = fgetc(f)) != EOF`, `(*p)++`, `(*arr)[i]`, `p->x` not `*p.x`.
- Use the course names and conventions: `size_t` with `%zu`, `int main(void)`, `struct tag` (not a typedef) unless the question gives one, `qstr_`/`qlstack_` style function names.
